title: Stabilize Calendar time references and preserve aggregate meaning
problem: Calendar X is based on live periods; full/current Y reference planning can depend on length checks and capped recursive plans. Missing, invalid and zero buckets have meaningful distinctions that generic time-series changes could erase.
proposal: Derive Calendar X from full chart-source periods across facets and honor explicit time view limits without filtering. Compute full/current bucket extrema at the displayed facet-by-split-by-period grain outside display caps, then union extrema across facets; never combine separate facet buckets into one aggregate. Allow filtered sums/averages to expand Y above the full reference, with explicit limits taking precedence. Preserve interval/contributor trace, count/sum zero-fill policy, average missingness and linear shared-scale areas/stacks.

title: Keep React, TypeScript and D3; allow one measured renderer spike only if needed
problem: Industrial UX and library multi-axis APIs establish useful patterns, but do not prove that replacing the current renderer would preserve filters, original trace, Notes, drafts, undo and exports or improve the required workload.
proposal: Retain the current React/TypeScript/D3 foundation. Implement and measure the accepted fidelity and interaction contract first. Reopen a renderer decision only after a worthwhile workload fails a documented gate despite bounded repair. Compare the current renderer with one pinned candidate on identical data, state, accessibility and source-evidence requirements; verify the chosen version license/embedding terms then. uPlot is a possible density spike and Highcharts a possible accessible-navigation spike, not selected dependencies.
